findings.title: Incorrect permission check logic
findings.explanation: The condition `if user.is_admin or user.id != document.owner_id:` allows editing when the user is not the owner (and not an admin) and blocks the owner, which is opposite of the intended behavior described in the docstring.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the condition to `if not (user.is_admin or user.id == document.owner_id):` and raise the error in that branch, or invert the logic accordingly.

findings.title: Document changes are not persisted to the database
findings.explanation: The function updates the document's body attribute but never calls `document.save()`, so the modification will not be saved in the database. Callers expecting the change to be persisted will see stale data.

findings.title: Incorrect permission check allows unauthorized edits
findings.explanation: The condition `if user.is_admin or user.id != document.owner_id:` returns for admins **or** any user whose ID is not the owner, effectively granting edit rights to anyone who is not the owner. This bypasses the intended access control and lets unauthorized users edit documents.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the logical operator to `and` so that only admins or the document owner are allowed: `if user.is_admin or user.id == document.owner_id:`

findings.title: Confusing edit permission check logic
findings.explanation: The condition `if user.is_admin or user.id != document.owner_id:` allows non‑owner, non‑admin users to pass and returns, which is the opposite of the intended logic. This makes the code hard to understand and error‑prone.
findings.suggested_fix:
Rewrite the condition to explicitly check for allowed users, e.g.
```python
if not user.is_admin and user.id != document.owner_id:
    raise PermissionError(...)
```

**high** · bug · Incorrect permission check logic

The condition `if user.is_admin or user.id != document.owner_id:` allows editing when the user is not the owner (and not an admin) and blocks the owner, which is opposite of the intended behavior described in the docstring.

**Suggested fix:** Change the condition to `if not (user.is_admin or user.id == document.owner_id):` and raise the error in that branch, or invert the logic accordingly.

**medium** · bug · Document changes are not persisted to the database

The function updates the document's body attribute but never calls `document.save()`, so the modification will not be saved in the database. Callers expecting the change to be persisted will see stale data.

**Suggested fix:** Add `document.save(update_fields=["body"])` before returning the document.
